subject.title: Browser-heavy sessions block all main lanes — need dedicated browser lane or per-channel lane routing

question: Should OpenClaw add first-class workload/channel lane routing for foreground embedded runs, and should the permanent shape be browser-specific, per-channel/per-agent, or a general server-owned lane policy with global caps?
rationale: The source proves the shared-main contention shape, but choosing a new public lane/config model changes scheduler semantics and compatibility-sensitive config surface.

options.title: General server-owned lane policy
options.body: Add a generic lane-routing model for foreground runs that derives allowed lanes from server config/capabilities and enforces global caps across custom lanes.

options.title: Narrow browser lane
options.body: Add only browser/workload classification first, which directly addresses this issue but may leave per-agent and per-channel starvation requests with a second API later.

options.title: Fold into existing scheduler issues
options.body: Close or narrow this issue under the per-agent and follow-up fairness trackers, accepting that browser/workload-class routing may not get its own explicit contract.

recommendation.title: General server-owned lane policy
recommendation.body: Add a generic lane-routing model for foreground runs that derives allowed lanes from server config/capabilities and enforces global caps across custom lanes.

likelyOwner.reason: His history covers the original queue model, queue modes, lane enum refactor, current lane resolver, and gateway lane setup.
